sections.heading: 4. What the Services do
sections.body:
{{shortName}} is a **collection management and market-information tool** for trading card and collectible hobbyists. Depending on your plan and platform, the Services let you:

- **Build a collection.** Add cards and sealed products to one or more collections ("vaults"), record quantity, condition, grade, purchase price, purchase date, notes, and custom tags.
- **See estimated values.** View estimated market values for the items you hold, aggregated from third-party marketplaces and price data providers, together with portfolio totals, profit-and-loss figures, historical charts, and analytics.
- **Scan and identify cards.** Photograph a card with your device camera (or upload an image) so we can attempt to identify it using optical character recognition, perceptual image hashing, and machine-learning image matching.
- **Pre-screen condition with Loupe Grade.** Get a non-binding estimate of centring and condition, and an indicative view of potential graded value. **This is not a grading service.** See Section 7 and the [Market Data & Valuation Disclosure]({{website}}/legal/disclosure).
- **Browse a catalog and marketplaces.** Search card catalogs, view set checklists and progress, and follow links out to third-party marketplaces where items may be listed for sale.
- **Set price alerts and watchlists.** Ask to be notified when an item crosses a price threshold.
- **Generate statements.** Produce periodic PDF statements summarising your collection.
- **Join the community.** Claim a public username, publish a profile, follow other collectors, and share collections, subject to your privacy settings.
- **Find local shops.** See card and game shops near a location you provide, and leave reviews.

**We are not a marketplace.** {{shortName}} does not sell, buy, broker, escrow, authenticate, appraise, insure, ship, or take custody of any card, collectible, or other item. We are not a party to any transaction you enter into with any third party, including any transaction you reach through a link in the Services. Any purchase, sale, trade, consignment, or grading submission you make is solely between you and the other party.

**Changes to the Services.** We are actively developing {{shortName}}. We may add, change, suspend, or discontinue any part of the Services at any time. Where a change materially and adversely affects a paid feature you are then paying for, Section 5 governs your remedy.

This section is fundamental to your use of the Services. Our full disclosure is at [Market Data & Valuation Disclosure]({{website}}/legal/disclosure), and is incorporated here.

**Estimates, not appraisals.** Every price, value, portfolio total, gain/loss figure, chart, trend, ranking, and analytic in the Services is an **automated estimate** derived from third-party sources. It is **not** an appraisal, a valuation opinion, a certification, a guarantee, an offer, a solicitation, or a commitment by anyone to buy or sell anything at that or any price.

**Sources and accuracy.** We aggregate data from third-party marketplaces, price guides, and catalog providers. That data may be **stale, delayed, incomplete, mismatched to the wrong item, wrong for your item's condition, language, edition, or printing, or simply inaccurate.** We do not independently verify it and we do not warrant it. Actual realisable value depends on condition, authenticity, grade, market timing, fees, shipping, taxes, and the specific buyer — none of which we can observe.

**Not financial, investment, tax, or legal advice.** {{shortName}} is an information and record-keeping tool. Nothing in the Services is investment advice, a recommendation, or an offer with respect to any security, commodity, or investment. **Collectible trading cards are not securities and are not regulated investments; they are illiquid, volatile, and can lose all of their value.** We are not a registered investment adviser, broker-dealer, appraiser, or insurance provider, and no fiduciary or advisory relationship is created by your use of the Services. Consult a qualified professional before making financial decisions.

**Loupe Grade is a pre-screen, not a grade.** The "Loupe Grade" feature produces an **indicative, non-binding, algorithmic estimate** of centring and surface condition from photographs you supply, and may show an indicative "upside" figure based on estimated graded prices. It is:

- **not** a professional grading, authentication, or certification service;
- **not** a prediction of, or substitute for, the grade any grading company would assign; and
- **not** endorsed by, affiliated with, or issued in cooperation with **Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA), Beckett Grading Services (BGS), Certified Guaranty Company (CGC), Sportscard Guaranty (SGC)**, or any other grading company.

Grading outcomes depend on factors no photograph can capture. **Do not submit a card for grading, buy, sell, insure, or price an item in reliance on a Loupe Grade result.**

**Card identification is probabilistic.** Our scanning and identification features return **best-guess candidates with confidence scores.** They can and do misidentify cards, sets, editions, languages, printings, and variants. **You are responsible for verifying that any item added to your collection is the item you actually own.**

**Your decisions are your own.** You are solely responsible for every buying, selling, trading, grading, insuring, tax, and record-keeping decision you make. **To the maximum extent permitted by law, we are not liable for any loss arising from your reliance on any value, estimate, grade, identification, alert, statement, or analytic in the Services.**

**Statements are not tax or accounting documents.** PDF statements and profit-and-loss figures are informational summaries generated from data you entered and estimates we computed. They are not audited, are not prepared to any accounting standard, and are not a substitute for records prepared by a qualified accountant. Cost basis, holding period, and taxable gain must be determined by you and your advisers.

- **Photo library.** Used only for images you explicitly choose to upload.
- **Location (when in use).** Used to find card and game shops near you and to show local listings. Coordinates are sent to our servers to run the shop search. We do not track your location in the background and we do not build a location history from it. See the [Privacy Policy]({{website}}/legal/privacy).
- **Notifications.** Used to deliver price alerts, security notices, and product updates you have opted into. You can turn notifications off in the app or in your device settings.

**Over-the-air updates.** The mobile apps may download and apply over-the-air updates to the application bundle. By using the apps you consent to receiving these updates automatically.

sections.heading: 2. Our commitments
sections.body:
These are commitments, not aspirations. If we ever change one, we will tell you before it takes effect.

1. **We do not sell your personal information**, and we do not "share" it for cross-context behavioural advertising, as those terms are defined under California and other US state privacy laws.
2. **We do not run advertising** in the Services, and we do not embed any third-party advertising or marketing SDK.
3. **We do not use third-party behavioural-analytics or attribution SDKs.** Our product analytics are computed on our own servers from data we already hold to run the Services.
4. **We do not disclose your collection contents or holdings to any data broker, insurer, marketplace, or advertiser.**
5. **The catalog and price providers we query receive card identifiers, not your identity** — see Section 8.
6. **We collect what a collection-tracking app needs to work**, and we delete it when it is no longer needed for that purpose.
7. **We never ask for, and never want, your payment card number.** Card payments are handled entirely by our payment processor.

sections.heading: 3. The personal data we collect
sections.body:
### 3.1 Account and identity data

| Data | Detail | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Email address | Required to create and recover an account, and to send transactional email | You |
| Password | Stored **only** as an Argon2id hash — we never store or can read your password | You |
| Display name, avatar image | Optional profile details | You, or Apple/Google at sign-in |
| Apple / Google subject identifier | An opaque per-app identifier returned by Sign in with Apple or Google. **We never receive your Apple or Google password.** | Apple, Google |
| Email verification status and timestamp | Whether you clicked the confirmation link | Derived |
| Two-factor authentication (2FA) secret and recovery codes | Only if you enable 2FA. The secret is encrypted at rest; recovery codes are stored as hashes and consumed on use | You |
| Failed sign-in count, temporary lockout time, session-revocation counter | Brute-force protection and "sign out everywhere" | Derived |
| Administrative role flag, ban status and reason | Account state | Us |

### 3.2 Subscription and billing data

| Data | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Plan (free / Pro), Pro start date, trial status, expiry | Held by us to determine your entitlements |
| Payment processor customer ID and subscription ID | Opaque Stripe identifiers linking your account to your subscription |
| Purchase and renewal events, invoices, receipts | Received from the payment processor |

**We do not receive, store, or have any access to your payment card number, expiry date, or security code.** Card details are collected and stored by **Stripe, Inc.** on its own PCI-DSS compliant systems. If you subscribe through the Apple App Store or Google Play, billing data is held by Apple or Google, and we receive only subscription status.

### 3.3 Collection and portfolio data

This is the substance of the product, and it is the data you give us most deliberately.

- Collections ("vaults") you create, their names, and which one is active
- Cards and sealed products you add: catalog identifier, game, set, card number, quantity, language, edition, printing
- Condition, grade, grading company, certification number, and subgrades you record
- Purchase price, purchase date, and cost basis you enter
- Free-text notes and custom tags you attach to a holding
- Watchlist entries and price alerts (item, threshold, direction, whether triggered)
- Point-in-time portfolio value snapshots we compute so your charts have history
- Set-completion progress derived from what you own
- Generated PDF statements and the storage keys pointing to them
- Recently viewed cards and recent searches (used to populate your "recent" rails)

### 3.4 Scan, image, and identification data

When you photograph or upload a card:

| Data | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| The image itself | Stored in our object storage under a key linked to the scan job |
| A small derived thumbnail | Retained so the scan history is reviewable |
| SHA-256 hash and perceptual hash of the image | Used to recognise a repeat scan instantly and skip re-processing |
| Text extracted by optical character recognition ("OCR") | The literal text read off the card, plus a confidence score |
| Parsed fields | Inferred card title, set code, card number, and game |
| Candidate matches and confidence scores | The ranked guesses we returned |
| Processing metadata | Provider used, latency, and our processing cost |
| Your feedback | Whether the top match was right, and which card you chose instead |
| Machine-learning image embedding | A numeric vector representing the card image, used for visual matching (feature-flagged) |

**These are photographs of trading cards, not of people.** We do not intentionally collect facial images, fingerprints, voiceprints, retina or iris scans, hand or face geometry, or any other **biometric identifier or biometric information**, and we do not use scan images for identity verification or facial recognition. **Please do not photograph people, identity documents, payment cards, or other sensitive material with the scanner.** If you do so accidentally, delete the scan and contact {{privacyEmail}}.

### 3.5 Community and social data

Only if you claim a username and use the community features:

- Username, biography, and any **free-text location you type** (for example "Brooklyn, NY"). **This is never derived from your GPS or IP address** — it is only what you choose to write.
- Profile picture you upload
- Whether your profile is private
- Who you follow, who follows you, and pending follow requests
- Profiles you liked, and profile visits (the profile owner may see that you visited)
- Shop reviews you write, the rating, and the shop they relate to
- Shops you save

### 3.6 Device, technical, and log data

| Data | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| IP address | Received with every request. Used for security, abuse prevention, and rate limiting, and recorded in the administrative audit log for privileged actions |
| Device and app information | Platform (iOS/Android/web), app and OS version, device model, locale, time zone |
| Push notification token | An opaque per-install token issued by the platform push service, plus the platform name |
| Server request logs | Timestamp, request path, status code, latency, and a request correlation identifier |
| Diagnostic and crash reports | Stack traces, breadcrumbs, and device state when an error occurs, captured by our error-monitoring provider |
| Session and authentication tokens | Held in your browser's local storage or your device's secure keychain |

### 3.7 Location data

If — and only if — you open the shop locator and grant location permission, your device sends **approximate or precise coordinates** to our servers so we can find shops near you.

- We use the coordinates to run that one search and to cache results **by geographic grid cell, not by user**.
- **We do not store a per-user location history, we do not track you in the background, and we do not use your location for advertising or profiling.**
- You can use the locator without granting permission by entering a place manually, and you can revoke the permission at any time in your device settings.

### 3.8 Communications data

- Emails we send you, including the **rendered content**, subject, recipient address, category, and delivery status (sent, delivered, bounced, complained). We keep the rendered copy so support and you can see exactly what was sent.
- Your email and notification preferences, including announcement opt-outs and suppression after a bounce or spam complaint
- Support messages you send us and our replies
- In-app notifications and their read state

### 3.9 AI feature data

If you use natural-language ("describe it") search or other AI-assisted features:

- The query text you typed, any game hint, the candidate names the model returned, the cards we matched, result count, latency, whether the answer came from cache, and any thumbs-up/down you give.

**Do not type personal or confidential information into an AI search box.** See Section 11.

### 3.10 Data we do not collect

For the avoidance of doubt, we do **not** collect: payment card numbers; government identification numbers; Social Security or national insurance numbers; precise background location; contacts, calendar, call logs, or SMS; health, genetic, or biometric data; racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, trade-union membership, or sexual orientation; advertising identifiers (IDFA/AAID); or cross-app tracking data. We do not operate any advertising or data-broker business.

sections.heading: 4. Where the data comes from
sections.body:
We collect personal data from four places, and no others:

1. **Directly from you** — what you type, upload, photograph, select, or configure.
2. **Automatically from your device** when you use the Services — IP address, device and app details, log and diagnostic data, and the permissions you grant.

**We do not buy personal data, we do not obtain it from data brokers, and we do not enrich or append to your profile from outside sources.**

Card catalog and pricing data we ingest from third-party providers is **information about cards, not about people**, and is not personal data.

sections.body:

| Purpose | Data used | Legal basis (GDPR Art. 6) |

| Provide the core product: store your collection, sync it across devices, compute values, charts, analytics, set progress, and statements | Collection and portfolio data, settings | **Contract** |

| Secure the Services: rate limiting, brute-force lockout, abuse and fraud detection, audit logging | IP address, log data, audit records | **Legitimate interests** in protecting our users and systems; **Legal obligation** where applicable |
| Diagnose crashes and errors, monitor performance and uptime | Diagnostic data, logs | **Legitimate interests** in a working, reliable product |
| Understand product usage in aggregate — engagement, retention, funnels | Aggregated event and account data | **Legitimate interests** in improving the product |
| Provide support and respond to your requests | Communications data, account data | **Contract**; **Legitimate interests** |
| Comply with law, respond to lawful requests, establish or defend legal claims | Whatever is strictly necessary | **Legal obligation**; **Legitimate interests** |

**Our legitimate-interests assessment.** Where we rely on legitimate interests, we have weighed our interest against your rights and freedoms and concluded that the processing is necessary, proportionate, and consistent with what you would reasonably expect from a collection-tracking app. **You have the right to object** — see Section 17. You can ask us for a summary of any assessment at {{privacyEmail}}.

**No processing for unrelated purposes.** We will not use your personal data for a materially different purpose without telling you first and, where required, obtaining your consent.

sections.heading: 6. We do not sell or share your personal information

**We have not sold or shared personal information in the preceding twelve (12) months, and we do not do so today.**

Specifically:

- We do not sell personal information for monetary or other valuable consideration.

If this ever changes, we will update this Policy, provide the notice the law requires **before** the change takes effect, and give you an opt-out mechanism.

We disclose personal data only in the situations below.

### 7.1 Service providers (processors)

We use a small number of vendors to run the Services. They act on our documented instructions, are bound by written data-processing terms, may not use your data for their own purposes, and must delete or return it when their engagement ends.

### 7.2 Other users, when you choose

Content you deliberately make public — your username, profile, avatar, bio, any location text you typed, collections you set to visible, and shop reviews you write — is visible to other users and, if your profile is public, to anyone on the internet. **You control this with your privacy settings.** Setting a profile to private removes it from public view going forward; it cannot retrieve copies others already made.

### 7.3 At your direction

If you export data, share a statement, or send a share link, the data goes wherever you send it.

### 7.4 Legal and safety disclosures

We may disclose personal data if we believe in good faith that it is reasonably necessary to:

- comply with a law, regulation, subpoena, court order, warrant, or other valid legal process;
- enforce our [Terms of Service]({{website}}/legal/terms) or investigate a potential violation;
- detect, prevent, or address fraud, security, or technical issues; or
- protect the rights, property, or safety of {{shortName}}, our users, or the public, including in an emergency involving a risk of death or serious physical injury.

**Our approach to legal demands.** Where we are legally permitted to do so, we will **notify you before disclosing your data** in response to a legal demand, so that you have an opportunity to challenge it, unless we are prohibited by law or a court order, or there is an emergency. We review demands for validity and scope and object to overbroad ones.

### 7.5 Corporate transactions

If we are involved in a merger, acquisition, financing, reorganisation, bankruptcy, or sale of all or part of our assets, personal data may be transferred as part of that transaction. **We will notify you before your personal data becomes subject to a materially different privacy policy**, and the acquirer will be bound by commitments at least as protective as those in this Policy until it does so.

### 7.6 Aggregated and de-identified data

We may create and use aggregated or de-identified data — for example, "cards most added this week" or "median value of Charizard holdings" — which does not identify you and is not personal data. **We maintain such data in de-identified form, do not attempt to re-identify it, and contractually require the same of anyone we give it to.**

### 7.7 Affiliates

We may share data with entities under common control with {{legalName}}, for the purposes described in this Policy and subject to it.

sections.heading: 8. Card catalog and price providers — what they do and don't receive
sections.body:
{{shortName}} draws card data and prices from a number of third-party catalog and pricing sources, listed in [Subprocessors & Data Sources]({{website}}/legal/subprocessors).

**What they receive:** a card identifier, set code, card name, or search term — that is, **information about a card**.

**What they do not receive:** your name, email address, account identifier, collection contents, portfolio value, or any other identifier that links a query to you. Requests are made **server-to-server from our infrastructure**, so these providers see our servers, not your device or IP address.

**Two deliberate exceptions**, both disclosed here:

1. **Card images** displayed in the app may be fetched by your device through our image proxy. The proxy sits between your device and the origin so that the origin sees our infrastructure, not you.
2. **Links you follow out** of {{shortName}} to a marketplace (for example an eBay or TCGplayer listing) are ordinary web navigations. **Once you tap through, that site sees your device and IP address and applies its own privacy policy.** We do not append your {{shortName}} identity to those links.

**Optical character recognition.** When our OCR provider is enabled, the **card image you scanned is transmitted to that provider** for text extraction. It is sent without your account identifier. See [Subprocessors & Data Sources]({{website}}/legal/subprocessors).

sections.heading: 9. Artificial intelligence and automated processing
sections.body:
**Where we use AI.** We use machine learning and large language models for: card identification from images (OCR, perceptual hashing, and image embeddings); natural-language card search; and internal tooling such as automatically designed browse shelves and administrative data queries.

**What is sent to AI providers.** For natural-language search, **the query text you typed** is sent to our AI provider along with instructions. Your account identifier, email, and collection contents are **not** sent. For card identification, the **card image** is sent to our OCR provider.

**Do not enter personal or confidential information** into an AI search box or any free-text field intended for card descriptions.

**Training.** **We do not permit our AI providers to train their models on your data.** We use enterprise/API tiers whose terms exclude training on submitted content. We may use scan images and identification feedback to improve **our own** card-matching models; where we do, we use them for that purpose only.

**No automated decisions with legal effect.** We do not make decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects about you based solely on automated processing, within the meaning of Article 22 of the GDPR. Automated processes such as free-tier limits, rate limiting, brute-force lockout, and abuse detection may restrict access to features; **you can always reach a human at {{supportEmail}}** to review any such restriction.

**AI output can be wrong.** Verify anything important. See the [Market Data & Valuation Disclosure]({{website}}/legal/disclosure).

sections.heading: 10. International data transfers
sections.body:
We are based in the **United States**, and our infrastructure and most of our service providers are located there. **If you use the Services from outside the United States, your personal data will be transferred to, stored in, and processed in the United States and potentially other countries** whose data-protection laws may differ from those of your own.

**Safeguards for EEA, UK, and Swiss transfers.** Where we transfer personal data out of the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or Switzerland, we rely on one or more of the following:

- the **European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses** (Decision 2021/914), together with the **UK International Data Transfer Addendum** and the Swiss adaptations, incorporated into our agreements with each processor;
- an **adequacy decision** covering the recipient country or certification framework, where one applies to that recipient; or
- a derogation under Article 49, where one genuinely applies.

**Transfer impact assessments.** We assess the laws of the destination country and the practical risk to your data, and apply supplementary measures — encryption in transit and at rest, access controls, minimisation, and a policy of challenging overbroad legal demands.

**Your copy.** You may request a copy of the relevant transfer safeguards, with commercial terms redacted, by emailing **{{privacyEmail}}**.

sections.heading: 12. How we protect your data
sections.body:
We maintain administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect personal data against unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, and destruction. These include:

- **Encryption in transit** using TLS for all connections, and **encryption at rest** for our databases and object storage.
- **Password hashing** with **Argon2id**, a memory-hard algorithm. Passwords are never stored or transmitted in a recoverable form, and we cannot read yours.
- **Optional two-factor authentication** using time-based one-time passwords, with one-time recovery codes stored as hashes. Where configured, 2FA secrets are sealed with an additional encryption key.
- **Brute-force protection**: temporary account lockout after repeated failed sign-in attempts.
- **Session revocation**: a per-account token version that lets you invalidate every outstanding session at once ("sign out everywhere").
- **Short-lived access tokens** with separate refresh tokens, signed with asymmetric keys.
- **Rate limiting** on authentication and sensitive endpoints.
- **Least-privilege access**: only personnel who need access to personal data to do their job have it, administrative access is role-gated, and **privileged administrative actions are logged, attributed, and retained**.
- **Secret management** via a managed secrets service; credentials are never stored in source code.
- **Server-side enforcement of entitlements** — the client is never trusted to decide what you may access.
- **Server-side proxying** of outbound requests, with protections against server-side request forgery.
- **Dependency and vulnerability monitoring**, and an automated security review of changes before release.

**No system is perfectly secure.** We cannot guarantee absolute security, and you share information at your own risk. **You can materially improve your own security** by using a unique, strong password, enabling 2FA, and signing out of shared devices.

**Breach notification.** If a personal-data breach occurs that is likely to result in a risk to your rights and freedoms, we will notify the relevant supervisory authority **within 72 hours** where the GDPR requires it, and notify affected individuals without undue delay where required by the GDPR or applicable US state breach-notification law.

**Reporting a vulnerability.** Please report security issues to **{{securityEmail}}**. We will not pursue legal action against good-faith security research conducted in accordance with our Acceptable Use Policy — do not access other users' data, do not degrade the Services, and give us reasonable time to fix the issue before disclosing it.

sections.heading: 14. Your rights in the EEA, the UK, and Switzerland
sections.body:
If you are in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or Switzerland, you have the following rights over your personal data:

- **Access** — obtain confirmation of whether we process your data, a copy of it, and information about the processing.
- **Rectification** — have inaccurate data corrected and incomplete data completed.
- **Erasure ("right to be forgotten")** — have your data deleted where one of the grounds in Article 17 applies.
- **Restriction** — have processing limited in the circumstances set out in Article 18.
- **Portability** — receive the data you provided to us in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format, and have it transmitted to another controller where technically feasible.
- **Object** — object at any time to processing based on our legitimate interests, on grounds relating to your particular situation. **You may object to direct marketing at any time, for any reason, and we will stop immediately.**
- **Withdraw consent** — where we rely on consent (for example, location access), withdraw it at any time. This does not affect the lawfulness of processing before withdrawal.
- **Not be subject to solely automated decisions** producing legal or similarly significant effects (see Section 9).
- **Lodge a complaint** with your local supervisory authority (see Section 21).

**How to exercise them.** Email **{{privacyEmail}}** from the address on your account, or use the in-app controls. **We respond within one month.** That period may be extended by two further months for complex or numerous requests, in which case we will tell you within the first month and explain why. **There is no charge**, unless a request is manifestly unfounded or excessive, in which case we may charge a reasonable fee or refuse — and we will explain our reasoning and your right to complain.

**Verification.** We will verify your identity before acting, proportionately to the sensitivity of the request. We may ask you to confirm from your account email address, or to sign in.

**Refusals.** If we cannot fulfil a request in whole or in part, we will tell you why and tell you how to challenge that decision.

sections.heading: 15. Your rights in the United States
sections.body:
Residents of **California, Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, Texas, Oregon, Montana, Delaware, Iowa, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Minnesota, Tennessee, Maryland, Rhode Island, Indiana, Kentucky**, and other states with comprehensive privacy laws have rights over their personal information. **We extend the rights below to every US resident, regardless of state**, because we would rather run one honest process than twenty.

**Your rights:**

- **Know / access** — what personal information we have collected about you, the categories of sources, the business or commercial purposes, the categories of third parties to whom we disclose it, and the specific pieces we hold.
- **Delete** — request deletion of personal information we collected from you, subject to the exceptions in the applicable statute.
- **Correct** — request correction of inaccurate personal information.
- **Portability** — receive a copy in a portable, readily usable format.
- **Opt out of sale, sharing, and targeted advertising** — **we do none of these**, so there is nothing to opt out of. If that ever changes, we will provide a "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information" link before it does.
- **Opt out of profiling** in furtherance of decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects — **we do not engage in such profiling**.
- **Limit the use of sensitive personal information** — **we do not collect or use sensitive personal information beyond the purposes permitted without an opt-out**.
- **Non-discrimination** — we will not deny you service, charge you a different price, or give you a lesser quality of service for exercising any of these rights. **We operate no financial-incentive programme.**
- **Appeal** — if we deny your request, you may appeal by replying to our decision or writing to {{privacyEmail}} with the subject "Privacy Appeal". **We will respond to an appeal within 45 days** with a written explanation. If we deny the appeal, we will tell you how to contact your state Attorney General.

**How to exercise them.** Email **{{privacyEmail}}**, or use the in-app controls in Section 13. **We respond within 45 days**, extendable once by a further 45 days where reasonably necessary, with notice to you.

**Authorised agents.** You may use an authorised agent. We will require written proof of authorisation and may require you to verify your own identity directly.

**Verification.** We verify requests by matching them to the email address on the account, or by asking you to sign in. We do not require you to create an account to make a request.

**California "Shine the Light" (Civ. Code § 1798.83).** We do not disclose personal information to third parties for their own direct-marketing purposes. There is therefore nothing to request under this statute, but you may confirm this at {{privacyEmail}}.

**Nevada (NRS 603A).** We do not sell covered information. Nevada residents may submit a verified opt-out request to {{privacyEmail}}.

sections.heading: 17. Children's privacy

documents.title: Cookie Policy
documents.lead: Every cookie and browser storage key {{shortName}} uses, what it does, and how to get rid of it.
summary: We set no advertising cookies and no third-party tracking cookies.
Almost everything we store is strictly necessary: your session and your interface preferences.
Nothing we store is used to profile you or follow you to other websites.

sections.heading: 1. What this policy covers
sections.body:
This Cookie Policy explains how **{{legalName}}** uses cookies and similar technologies — including **browser local storage**, **session storage**, and **mobile secure storage** — on the {{shortName}} website at {{website}}, in the {{shortName}} web application, and in the {{shortName}} mobile apps.

It should be read with our [Privacy Policy]({{website}}/legal/privacy), which explains how we handle personal data generally.

**The short version: we use the minimum a signed-in web app needs, and nothing more.** We do not run advertising, we do not use third-party analytics or attribution tools in the client, and **we do not set any cookie that follows you to another website.**

sections.heading: 2. Cookies and similar technologies, briefly
sections.body:
A **cookie** is a small text file a website asks your browser to store and send back on later visits. **Local storage** and **session storage** are similar browser stores, but the data is read by the page's own code rather than sent automatically with every request. On mobile, the operating system provides an encrypted **keychain** or **keystore** for secrets.

A **first-party** cookie is set by the site you are visiting. A **third-party** cookie is set by a different company, and is the mechanism behind cross-site tracking and advertising. **{{shortName}} sets no third-party cookies.**

sections.heading: 3. Exactly what we store
sections.body:
### Strictly necessary — the app does not work without these

| Name / purpose | Type | What it does | Lifetime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Session / access token | Local storage (web); encrypted keychain or keystore (mobile) | Keeps you signed in and authorises your requests. **Without it you would be signed out on every page load.** | Until you sign out, the token expires, or you clear your browser |
| Refresh token | Local storage (web); encrypted secure storage (mobile) | Renews your short-lived access token without making you sign in again | Until you sign out or revoke your sessions |
| Sign-in intent ("nav key") | Session storage | Remembers what you were trying to do when we asked you to sign in, so we can return you there afterwards | Cleared when you close the tab |
| CSRF / request correlation identifiers | In-memory and request headers | Ties a request to its response for security and support diagnostics | The request |

### Functional — remembered preferences

| Name / purpose | Type | What it does | Lifetime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Theme preference | Local storage | Remembers light, dark, or system appearance | Until cleared |
| Display currency | Local storage, mirrored to your profile | Remembers which currency to show values in | Until cleared |
| Active collection | Local storage, mirrored to your profile | Remembers which vault you were viewing | Until cleared |
| Recent searches and recently viewed cards | Local storage | Populates your "recent" rails. **Stored on your device**; you can clear it from those rails | Up to 12 months, or until cleared |
| Dismissed banners and completed onboarding | Local storage | Stops us showing you the same announcement or tour twice | Until cleared |
| Cached API responses | In-memory and local storage | Makes the app fast and reduces data usage | Minutes to hours |

### Diagnostics — only if enabled

| Name / purpose | Type | What it does | Lifetime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Error-monitoring session identifier | Local storage | Groups the events of one browsing session so a crash report is intelligible. Set only when error monitoring is enabled, and it carries no advertising identifier | Session |

### What we do not use

- **No advertising or retargeting cookies.**
- **No third-party analytics, attribution, heat-mapping, or session-replay tools.**
- **No social media tracking pixels** (no Meta pixel, no TikTok pixel, no LinkedIn Insight tag).
- **No fingerprinting** of your device or browser for tracking purposes.
- **No mobile advertising identifiers** (no IDFA, no Android Advertising ID). The apps do not request App Tracking Transparency permission.

sections.heading: 4. Consent
sections.body:
**Strictly necessary storage** — your session and the security items above — is exempt from consent requirements under the EU ePrivacy Directive and equivalent laws, because the service you requested cannot be provided without it.

**Functional and diagnostic storage** is either exempt on the same basis, or set only after you take an action that plainly implies it (choosing a theme, running a search).

**Because we set no advertising or third-party tracking storage, we do not show a cookie consent banner.** We consider a banner that asks for consent we do not need to be noise, not privacy. If we ever introduce non-essential tracking, **we will implement a proper consent mechanism with a genuine "reject all" option before doing so**, and update this Policy first.

sections.heading: 5. How to see and clear what we store
sections.body:
**In your browser.** Open developer tools and inspect Application → Local Storage / Session Storage / Cookies for {{website}} to see exactly what is there. Every major browser also lets you clear site data:

- **Safari** — Settings → Privacy → Manage Website Data
- **Chrome** — Settings → Privacy and security → Third-party cookies / Site data
- **Firefox** — Settings → Privacy & Security → Cookies and Site Data
- **Edge** — Settings → Cookies and site permissions

**What happens when you clear it.** You will be **signed out**, and your theme, currency, recent searches, and dismissed banners will reset. **Nothing in your account is deleted** — your collection lives on our servers, not in your browser.

**Blocking storage entirely** will prevent you from signing in, because we cannot keep you authenticated without somewhere to keep the token.

**On mobile.** Delete the app, or use Settings → Account → Sign out, to clear stored credentials from the device keychain.

**Global Privacy Control.** See Section 18 of our [Privacy Policy]({{website}}/legal/privacy).

sections.heading: 6. Why we use local storage for your session
sections.body:
We want to be straight with you about a technical trade-off.

The web app currently keeps your session token in **browser local storage** rather than in an `HttpOnly` cookie. Local storage is readable by JavaScript running on the page, which means a successful cross-site scripting attack against our own site could read it — an `HttpOnly` cookie could not be read that way.

**What we do about it:** we serve a strict Content Security Policy and related security headers designed to prevent injected script from executing at all; we keep access tokens short-lived; we bind them to a session version so every token can be revoked instantly; and we offer two-factor authentication.

**What we are doing about it:** migrating session handling to `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite` cookies is on our roadmap. We will update this section when it ships. We would rather tell you this than let you assume otherwise.

sections.heading: 7. Changes and contact
sections.body:
We will update this Policy when our use of cookies and similar technologies changes, with a revised "Last updated" date. **If we ever add non-essential tracking, we will tell you and ask for consent before we do.**

sections.heading: 1. About this page
sections.body:
This page forms part of our [Privacy Policy]({{website}}/legal/privacy). It lists the third parties {{legalName}} engages to operate {{shortName}}.

We distinguish two very different kinds of third party:

1. **Subprocessors** — vendors that **process personal data on our behalf**, under a written data-processing agreement that limits them to our instructions, requires appropriate security, restricts onward transfers, and obliges them to delete or return the data when we stop using them.
2. **Data sources** — providers we query for **information about cards**. They receive card identifiers and search terms. **They do not receive your name, email address, account identifier, collection contents, or portfolio value.** Queries are made server-to-server from our infrastructure, so these providers see our servers, not your device.

**Notice of change.** We will update this page **before** adding a new subprocessor that processes personal data, or at the latest when it begins processing. To be notified of changes, email **{{privacyEmail}}** with the subject "Subprocessor notifications" and we will add you to the list. If you object to a new subprocessor on reasonable data-protection grounds, contact us and we will work with you in good faith; if we cannot resolve it, you may stop using the Services and we will refund any prepaid unused fees.

sections.heading: 4. Our own infrastructure

documents.title: Market Data & Valuation Disclosure
documents.lead: What {{shortName}}'s prices, portfolio values, and Loupe Grade results actually are — and, more importantly, what they are not.
summary: Every value in {{shortName}} is an automated estimate, not an appraisal and not an offer.
Loupe Grade is a photographic pre-screen. It is not a grade, and we are not affiliated with PSA, BGS, CGC, or SGC.
Trading cards are not investments, not securities, and not regulated. They are illiquid and can lose all their value.
Card identification is probabilistic and can be wrong. Verify before you rely on it.

sections.heading: 1. Why this page exists
sections.body:
{{shortName}} shows you numbers: what a card is "worth", what your collection totals, whether you are up or down, what a graded copy might fetch. Those numbers look precise. **They are estimates, and treating them as facts will cost you money.**

This disclosure explains, honestly and specifically, how each figure is produced and where it breaks down. It forms part of our [Terms of Service]({{website}}/legal/terms) and is incorporated into Section 7 of those Terms.

**Read this before you make any decision involving real money.**

sections.heading: 2. How we produce a price
sections.body:
We do not set prices and we do not observe transactions ourselves. For each card, we:

1. **Match** your item to a catalog entry, using its identifier, set, number, language, and printing.
2. **Query** one or more third-party price sources — marketplaces, price guides, and aggregators — listed in [Subprocessors & Data Sources]({{website}}/legal/subprocessors).
3. **Select** a figure from the available sources according to a **fallback chain**: where our preferred source has no data, or our subscription tier with that source does not include the field, we fall back to the next source.
4. **Cache** the result, sometimes for hours, to stay within the metered terms on which that data is licensed to us.
5. **Convert** to your display currency using a foreign-exchange rate that is itself periodically refreshed.

**Every one of those five steps can introduce error.**

sections.heading: 3. Where it goes wrong — specifically
sections.body:
We would rather tell you the failure modes than let you discover them.

- **Staleness.** A displayed price may be **hours or days old**. In a moving market it can be badly wrong. A flat line on a chart usually means **missing data points, not a calm market**.
- **Wrong match.** Automated matching can attach the wrong catalog entry to your item, especially across **languages, regional printings, reprints, promos, error cards, and variants**. A Japanese card priced as its English counterpart is a real and common failure.
- **Condition blindness.** Unless you record a condition or grade, a figure generally reflects some notional near-mint copy. **Your played copy is worth substantially less.**
- **Grade blindness.** Where graded prices are unavailable from our sources, a graded value may be **modelled from a raw price rather than observed**. Modelled figures are labelled where we can, but treat any graded value as indicative.
- **Thin markets.** For scarce cards, a "price" may rest on **one or two sales**, or on an asking price nobody paid. Asking prices are not sale prices.
- **Sealed product** is priced from a different and often sparser source set than singles.
- **Currency conversion** adds its own error, and the rate you actually get will differ.
- **Costs are excluded.** Displayed values are **gross**. Real proceeds are reduced by marketplace fees, payment fees, shipping, insurance, grading fees, and tax — frequently **15% to 30%** of the headline number, sometimes more.
- **Source outages.** When an upstream provider is down, rate-limits us, or withdraws access, values can go stale, disappear, or revert to an older figure with no visible warning.
- **Aggregation error.** A portfolio total inherits every error in every item it contains, and mixes items priced from different sources on different dates.

sections.heading: 4. What this is not
sections.body:
**Not an appraisal.** Nothing in {{shortName}} is an appraisal, valuation opinion, or certification. We are not appraisers. **Do not submit a {{shortName}} figure or statement to an insurer, lender, court, or tax authority as though it were an independent professional appraisal.**

**Not an offer.** No figure is an offer, solicitation, or commitment by us or anyone else to buy or sell anything at any price. **We do not buy, sell, broker, escrow, authenticate, or take custody of cards.**

**Not investment advice.** {{shortName}} is a record-keeping and information tool. Nothing in it is investment, financial, tax, accounting, or legal advice, or a recommendation to buy, hold, or sell anything. **We are not a registered investment adviser, broker-dealer, appraiser, or insurance provider**, and no fiduciary or advisory relationship arises from your use of the Services.

**Trading cards are not investments in the regulated sense.** They are **not securities**, are not covered by investor-protection regimes, are **illiquid**, carry authenticity and condition risk, and are exposed to reprints, set rotations, market sentiment, and changes in publisher policy. **You can lose everything you put in.** Past appreciation says nothing about the future.

**Not accounting records.** Statements and profit-and-loss figures are informational summaries built from data you entered and estimates we computed. They are **unaudited**, are not prepared to any accounting standard, and are **not a substitute for records prepared by a qualified accountant**. You and your advisers are responsible for determining cost basis, holding period, and taxable gain.

sections.heading: 5. Loupe Grade — read this carefully
sections.body:
**Loupe Grade produces an algorithmic estimate from photographs. It is not a grade.**

**What it is.** A pre-screen. It measures apparent centring from the image, applies a condition heuristic, and returns an **indicative estimate** together with an indicative view of what a high-grade copy might be worth.

**What it is not:**

- It is **not** a professional grading, authentication, or certification service.
- It is **not** a prediction of the grade any grading company would assign.
- It is **not** endorsed by, affiliated with, licensed by, or produced in cooperation with **Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA)**, **Beckett Grading Services (BGS)**, **Certified Guaranty Company (CGC)**, **Sportscard Guaranty (SGC)**, or any other grading company. We have no relationship with any of them.
- It **cannot** assess authenticity, trimming, recolouring, cleaning, pressing, or any other alteration.
- It **cannot** see surface scratches, print lines, gloss loss, dimples, edge wear, or corner softness that a photograph does not capture, and it is **highly sensitive to lighting, focus, angle, and background**.

**Real grading depends on factors no photograph can capture**, and on human judgement that varies between graders and over time.

**Do not** submit a card for grading, buy, sell, insure, price, or represent an item to anyone in reliance on a Loupe Grade result. **Do not tell a buyer that a card "is a PSA 10" or "will grade a 10" on the basis of a Loupe Grade result** — doing so may be a misrepresentation for which you, not we, are responsible. See Section 3 of the [Acceptable Use Policy]({{website}}/legal/acceptable-use).

**"PSA-10 upside" figures** are arithmetic on estimated graded prices. They are **not** a forecast, and they do not account for grading fees, shipping, insurance, turnaround time, or the substantial probability that the card does not achieve that grade.

sections.heading: 6. Card identification and scanning
sections.body:
Our scanner returns **ranked candidates with confidence scores**, produced by optical character recognition, perceptual image hashing, and machine-learning image matching.

**It is probabilistic and it will sometimes be wrong** — particularly for cards that look similar, for **reprints and alternate printings**, across **languages**, for **error and variant cards**, for holographic surfaces under difficult lighting, and for damaged cards.

**A high confidence score is not a guarantee.**

**You are responsible for verifying** that anything added to your collection is the item you actually own. Check the set symbol, the collector number, the language, the copyright line, and the printing before you rely on a value.

Some games in the app have **catalog data but no price feed** at all. Where that is the case, values will be absent rather than estimated.

sections.heading: 7. Price alerts, charts, and analytics
sections.body:
**Alerts are best-effort.** They depend on price data refreshing, on our schedulers running, and on your device accepting a notification. **They may fire late, fire on stale data, or not fire at all.** Do not build a trading strategy on them.

**Charts show our recorded snapshots**, not a continuous market record. Gaps, flat segments, and step changes usually reflect **when we managed to record a value**, not what the market did. Historical coverage begins when we started recording for that item, not when the card was printed.

**Analytics, trends, movers, and rankings** are derived from the same estimated data and inherit every limitation above. Rankings can be dominated by a single mispriced item.

sections.heading: 8. Your responsibility, and our liability
sections.body:
**Every buying, selling, trading, grading, insuring, tax, and record-keeping decision you make is yours.** Verify independently — check recent completed sales on the marketplace you would actually use, in your item's exact condition, language, and printing, and subtract the fees you would actually pay.

**Consult a qualified professional** — an appraiser, accountant, tax adviser, or attorney — before acting on anything of consequence.

**To the maximum extent permitted by law, {{legalName}} is not liable for any loss arising from your reliance on any price, value, estimate, grade, identification, alert, chart, statement, or analytic in the Services.** See Sections 20 and 21 of the [Terms of Service]({{website}}/legal/terms), which limit our liability and which you should read alongside this page.
